mentl/4a47110:
The banked probe read the last unread piece of the 39-line diff:
parse_int's own body, 72 lines in m2 and 71 in m3. The missing line is
`(local.set $go (local.get $state_tmp))`, the binding of the freshly
allocated closure record to the local named after the nested fn, while
`(local.get $go)` two instructions later survives. A wasm local defaults
to zero, so the closure handed to the tail call is a null pointer, its fn
index is garbage, and return_call_indirect through ft3 mismatches. That
is the trap end to end, and the first account in this sub-arc that
actually explains it.

The defect is the Carried-Truth Law at the emitter. One nested fn is
reached through two name computations: the table-index global emits
qualified as parse_int_go_idx, the local binding emits bare as go. When
the discriminator starts qualifying, the global follows and the local.set
vanishes while its reader does not. The same fact derived twice, and the
derivations disagree.

It is latent and has nothing to do with rows. Any change that makes a
nested fn's name qualify drops that fn's closure binding. The row arc
merely tripped it, which is why six explanations about rows, sorts,
readers, symbols, indices and tables all died first.

What this cost, stated so the shape is legible: seven probes to reach a
one-line diff that was inside the first emit-diff report. That report
said "named wheel fns differing (structural, 3)" on its second line and I
read the rename list beneath it instead. The instrument was right the
first time; the reading was not.

Next step is a build with a precise target: the emit site that writes a
nested fn's closure local.set must read the same name the index global
reads. The allocator arms are not it, since they emit local.set target
from a call to alloc, and the dropped line binds an already-allocated
record — so the site is the let-binding path.

Boot unchanged; docs only.

mentl/4ad2af4:
The row algebra's mirror, landed whole across both layers: nesting is
short-circuit AND, alternation is short-circuit OR, tags/literals are
atomic predicates, wildcards/vars are true. A match is an ordered
OR-ELSE fold; every arm emits (pred)(if (then binds body)(else rest)).

Each constructor's predicate carries its OWN representation guard
(nullary = sentinel compare; fielded = scrut>=heap_base before the tag
load), which dissolves the entire arm-set shape system: MatchShape ADT,
classify_arms_shape, emit_match_arms_uniform/mixed, the runtime
heap_base threshold fork, filter_arms_by_shape — deleted in both the
wheel emitter and the seed (ec5 family). Mixed matches, cross-shape
alternation, tuple/record/list arms (previously SILENTLY DROPPED), and
nested sentinel/fielded sub-patterns all compose from ONE predicate
projection + ONE binds projection. List-rest binds in match position
emit slice() — closes Hβ.emit.list-pattern-match-dispatch (06511f6's
named follow-up). Guard elision when the scrutinee type proves all-
fielded is a gradient cash-out, not a shape system.

The probe that first looked for this read the DOM the same way and reported the bug in the wrong place, which is worth remembering. An exported issue carried an empty orange box at the bottom of the page that never went away. pageWithSeed clones the live document and empties the containers the app rebuilds on boot, but a toast that was showing at the moment of export kept its inline display:block through the clone, so the file shipped it visible with nothing in it. Inline style comes off every emptied container now, and body loses whatever classes the running page had hung on it, so what ships is the page as built and not the page as it happened to be at the instant somebody pressed export. The fit meter moved to its own file to keep the press under the line ceiling. Both bugs are asserted: the back cover keeps its line breaks through a bell rung from the desk, and the file that lands on the next machine has nothing half-shown from the one that made it.
